user.title: Pair a Windows PC
user.description: Choose the connection selected in WHAT > Settings > Home Assistant Installations. WHAT API supports both local and remote connections without a broker. MQTT uses the broker configured in Home Assistant's MQTT integration.

reconfigure.title: Reconfigure this PC
reconfigure.description: Choose the connection selected in WHAT > Settings > Home Assistant Installations. WHAT API supports both local and remote connections without a broker. MQTT uses the broker configured in Home Assistant's MQTT integration. Updating this entry keeps its device and entity IDs.

reauth_confirm.title: Update PC pairing
reauth_confirm.description: Choose the connection selected in WHAT > Settings > Home Assistant Installations. WHAT API supports both local and remote connections without a broker. MQTT uses the broker configured in Home Assistant's MQTT integration. Updating this entry keeps its device and entity IDs.

api.title: Pair using WHAT API
api.description: Copy the pairing details from WHAT > Settings > Home Assistant Installations > Pairing. For local access, enter the PC address and port. For remote access, leave the PC address blank and configure this Home Assistant's HTTPS address in WHAT. Both use the same WHAT API. Readings appear after the PC authenticates.

mqtt.title: Pair using MQTT
mqtt.description: Copy the pairing details from WHAT > Settings > Home Assistant Installations > Pairing. WHAT and Home Assistant's MQTT integration must use the same broker. Readings appear after the PC authenticates.

error.cannot_connect: Cannot connect. Check that WHAT is running, the address and port are correct, and Windows Firewall allows the connection.
error.invalid_auth: Pairing token rejected. Copy the current token from the PC app.
error.fingerprint_mismatch: Certificate mismatch. Copy the fingerprint directly from the intended PC; it may have been reset.
error.invalid_input: Enter the copied PC device ID, a PC name (up to 80 characters), a 64-character hexadecimal pairing token and the full certificate fingerprint. If using a local PC address, enter a hostname or IP without wss:// and a port from 1 to 65535.
error.invalid_protocol: The app protocol or device identity does not match. Check that both packages are compatible and this is the intended PC.
error.mqtt_not_configured: Home Assistant's MQTT integration is not ready. Set up or repair MQTT under Settings > Devices & services, then try again.
error.unknown: An unexpected error occurred while pairing. Check the Home Assistant logs for details.

abort.invalid_discovery: The discovered service did not provide a valid identity.
abort.unique_id_mismatch: This is a different PC. Add it as a separate WHAT integration.
abort.already_in_progress: Pairing is already in progress for this PC.
abort.incompatible_discovery: This PC advertises an incompatible WHAT protocol or does not support TLS. Update WHAT and its integration before pairing.

run_command.name: Run Windows command
run_command.description: Execute a command on one paired PC. Requires remote shell permission and Home Assistant administrator access for user calls. Commands and output may appear in automation traces.

shell.name: Shell
shell.description: Windows PowerShell, installed PowerShell 7, CMD or WSL.

command.name: Command
command.description: Up to 2048 characters. Runs non-interactively without requesting elevation.

timeout.name: Timeout
timeout.description: Maximum run time in seconds, from 1 to 300.

distribution.name: WSL distribution
distribution.description: Optional installed WSL distribution; omit to use the default. Requires the Linux timeout utility.

device_id.name: WHAT PC
device_id.description: The paired Windows PC that will receive this action.

leave_running.name: Leave launched apps running
leave_running.description: Keep child applications open after the shell exits successfully. Timeout, cancellation or failure still stops them. WHAT cannot cancel released applications later. Windows shells only, not WSL. Use Start-Process in PowerShell or start "" "app.exe" in CMD so the shell finishes instead of waiting for the app.

send_notification.name: Send Windows notification
send_notification.description: Send a notification to one PC. Images, replies, longer text and action buttons require installed WHAT. Windows notification settings may suppress it. Limited to one per second.

device_id.name: WHAT PC
device_id.description: The paired Windows PC that will receive this action.

title.name: Title
title.description: One line, up to 128 Windows text units. Emoji can count as two. Portable notifications allow 63.

message.name: Message
message.description: Up to 2000 Windows text units. Plain text; line breaks are allowed. Portable notifications allow 255.

level.name: Notification icon
level.description: Selects the icon; does not bypass Do not disturb.

notification_id.name: Notification ID
notification_id.description: Optional ID, up to 64 characters. Reusing it replaces the previous notification. Included in action events.

image.name: Image URL
image.description: HTTP or HTTPS image reachable from the PC, up to 2 MiB and 4096 pixels per side.

actions.name: Action buttons
actions.description: Up to four objects with id and title. Optional url opens a web page; other buttons fire what_notification_action in Home Assistant. OPEN is reserved for clicking the notification body.

reply.name: Include a reply box
reply.description: Add at least one action without a URL. Its click sends the reply text in the Home Assistant event.

silent.name: Silent
silent.description: Send without a notification sound. Windows notification settings still apply.

ttl.name: Expires after
ttl.description: Defaults to 600 seconds. Expired action clicks are ignored.

speak.name: Speak
speak.description: Speak on a PC using an installed Windows voice. Requires Speech and Audio permission in WHAT. Replaces the current announcement.

message.name: Message
message.description: The text to speak on the selected PC.

voice.name: Windows voice ID
voice.description: Optional installed voice ID, listed under Speech and Audio in WHAT. Omit for the Windows default voice.

rate.name: Speech rate
rate.description: Playback speed from 0.5 to 2. Use 1 for normal speed.

volume.name: Announcement volume
volume.description: WHAT player volume only. Does not change Windows master volume.

device_id.name: WHAT PC
device_id.description: The paired Windows PC that will receive this action.

send_keyboard.name: Send keyboard input
send_keyboard.description: Press a shortcut or type text into the active Windows window. Requires PC input permission and Home Assistant administrator access. Does not retry.

device_id.name: WHAT PC
device_id.description: The paired Windows PC that will receive this action.

keys.name: Shortcut keys
keys.description: Select modifiers first, then the key. Leave empty when sending text.

text.name: Text to type
text.description: Up to 1024 UTF-16 units. Leave keys empty. Text may appear in Home Assistant traces; not logged on the PC.

send_mouse.name: Send mouse input
send_mouse.description: Move or click at physical desktop pixel coordinates across all monitors. Negative coordinates are supported. Requires PC input permission and Home Assistant administrator access.

device_id.name: WHAT PC
device_id.description: The paired Windows PC that will receive this action.

x.name: X coordinate
x.description: Horizontal position in physical desktop pixels. Negative values address monitors left of the main display.

y.name: Y coordinate
y.description: Vertical position in physical desktop pixels. Negative values address monitors above the main display.

button.name: Mouse button
button.description: Choose a button to click, or none to move the pointer only.

clicks.name: Click count
clicks.description: Optional; defaults to one when a button is selected. Omit for movement only.

apply_display_layout.name: Apply display layout
apply_display_layout.description: Apply a staged arrangement from the WHAT display card. Requires administrator access and PC display-control permission. No automatic rollback or retry.

entity_id.name: Display arrangement sensor
entity_id.description: The display arrangement sensor belonging to the PC to change.

layout.name: Requested layout
layout.description: The requested monitor arrangement, generated by the WHAT display card.

expected.name: Original layout
expected.description: The arrangement before editing. A newer Windows layout causes rejection.

wallpaper_engine.name: Wallpaper Engine
wallpaper_engine.description: Control Wallpaper Engine on one PC. Requires the module and Home Assistant control permission in WHAT. Commands are not retried.

device_id.name: WHAT PC
device_id.description: The paired Windows PC that will receive this action.

operation.name: Operation
operation.description: The Wallpaper Engine action to run on the selected PC.

file.name: Wallpaper file
file.description: Wallpaper file path on the Windows PC, for openWallpaper.

playlist.name: Playlist
playlist.description: Saved Wallpaper Engine playlist name, for openPlaylist.

profile.name: Profile
profile.description: Saved display profile name, for openProfile.

monitor.name: Monitor
monitor.description: Wallpaper Engine monitor index (0 is the first). Omit for the operation's default target.

options.name: Options
options.description: Optional file, playlist, profile, monitor (0-based), location, preset, window parameters or properties object. Paths refer to the Windows PC.

certificate_mismatch.title: Verify the certificate for {name}
certificate_mismatch.description: The direct connection presented a different certificate. Open WHAT on the intended PC and copy its current certificate fingerprint. In Home Assistant, open the existing WHAT entry and choose Reconfigure. Verify the PC before accepting the new fingerprint. Keeping the existing entry preserves device and entity IDs. Other working connection routes remain available.

identity_mismatch.title: The address for {name} belongs to a different PC
identity_mismatch.description: WHAT rejected a connection because the PC identity did not match the paired device. Check the address and choose Reconfigure on the existing WHAT entry to restore the intended PC. Add a replacement PC as a separate entry; do not reuse this pairing for a different device.

protocol_mismatch.title: Update the WHAT components for {name}
protocol_mismatch.description: The Windows app and this integration use incompatible protocol versions. Install compatible releases of both components, then reconnect the PC. Keep the existing WHAT entry to preserve device and entity IDs.

invalid_data.title: Invalid WHAT data received from {name}
invalid_data.description: WHAT rejected a malformed update. Enable debug logging for this integration and download its diagnostics if the problem continues. Check that the Windows app and integration are compatible releases. The notice clears when this connection delivers a valid update.
